newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips up 1.7 pct on rebound, fund buying.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips up 1.7 pct on rebound, fund buying.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chip stocks were trading firmer on Tuesday on a technical rebound and institutional buying after Bank Negara's clarification of its measures to curb property lending, traders and analysts said.
At 0700 GMT the benchmark Composite Index was trading 19.2 points, 1.69 percent, higher at 1,153.43.
"The clarifications have left us a bit more bullish, espacially as the sell off last week was overdone," said Stephen Weller, director of strategy at Pesaka Jardine Fleming.

Local and U.S.-based funds were actively buying Malaysian blue chips, with some of the foreign institutional funds covering short-positions created last week during a sharp slide in share prices, traders said.
Malaysia's central bank clarified measures announced in March to curb lending for property purchases, which were seen leading to speculative activity within the sector.
"The teeth have been taken out of the tiger. The clarifications definitely raise the earnings estimates of property companies," said a dealer at a local bank-backed brokerage house.
At around 0750 GMT the composite Index was up 23 points to 1157.23, a 2.03 percent jump from Monday's close.

"The bank is still quite stern in its measures. It has not announced anything new, but has just clarified its stance. But it is quite clear the market fundamentals now look good. Fundamentally, stocks are now looking cheap," said Weller.

Telekom Malaysia rose 60 cents to 19.40 ringgit, mainly on the back of a technical rebound, analysts said. "I would not change my recommendation of a hold on the stock just because the stock has rebounded," said a telecommunications analyst.
